subject: history_social
passage: Mehrgarh, on the Kachi Plain of Balochistan in Pakistan, is one of the earliest known farming villages in South Asia; people there grew barley and herded goats more than 8,000 years ago. The site is also known for a less expected discovery. In 2006, researchers reported that eleven molars from graves dated to roughly 7,500 to 9,000 years ago had small, neat holes drilled into them. Because the edges of the holes had been worn smooth by later chewing, the researchers concluded that the drilling was done on living people, an early form of dentistry.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Mehrgarh is one of the earliest known farming villages in South Asia.
choices.B: Teeth found at Mehrgarh suggest that people there practiced an early form of dentistry.
choices.C: Researchers found that the teeth from Mehrgarh had been drilled after their owners died.
choices.D: Farming at Mehrgarh caused tooth decay that forced villagers to drill their teeth.

explanation.why: After one sentence of background on farming, the text turns to "a less expected discovery" and spends the rest on it: drilled molars whose worn edges show the drilling was done on living people, which researchers read as "an early form of dentistry." That discovery is the text's main point.
explanation.A: Incorrect. This is background from the first sentence; most of the text is about the drilled teeth.
explanation.B: Correct. This captures the discovery the text focuses on and the conclusion the researchers drew from it.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The worn edges led researchers to conclude the opposite: the drilling was done while the people were alive.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text never says farming caused tooth decay or explains why the teeth were drilled.
